recent.text: Kyrie Irving scored 34 points, but Cleveland’s 28-9 run to close the first half left Dallas chasing in a 127-117 loss. “We didn’t match their desire and determination to compete,” Dusty May said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/EEUv9DRlk6
recent.author: Grant Afseth

recent.text: Dallas lost the second quarter 38-20 in Cleveland. Isolation defense and finding easier looks for Cooper Flagg were among the other issues. “We definitely didn’t play with the right level of urgency,” Dusty May said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/Vf3aUX6YpE
recent.author: Grant Afseth

recent.text: Cleveland rested Mitchell, Mobley, Harden, and Allen and still beat Dallas. Caleb Martin said the opponent’s lineup cannot change the approach. “It doesn’t matter who’s playing. They stick to the plan,” Martin said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/tVhN2ioe4I
recent.author: Grant Afseth

recent.text: Cleveland scored 23 points on 19 isolation possessions against Dallas, according to Synergy. “Our inability to guard one on one was the biggest issue,” Dusty May said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/xz5g1KUZU7
recent.author: Grant Afseth

recent.text: Kyrie Irving backed Dusty May’s criticism of the Mavericks’ urgency after the loss in Cleveland. “When your head coach is calling it out, that’s got to do something to you,” Irving said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/dEReCJNZuh
recent.author: Grant Afseth

recent.text: Tyrese Proctor had 24 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists against Dallas. Kyrie Irving praised his fellow former Duke guard afterward. “He played with a lot of confidence tonight, and he led their team,” Irving said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/rz35639zyc
recent.author: Grant Afseth

recent.text: Kyrie Irving reflected on arriving in Cleveland at 19 and learning to handle the expectations of being the No. 1 pick. “Don’t try to hide away from criticism. Don’t try to run away from it,” Irving said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/14IPO2wL8L

recent.text: Kyrie Irving reflected on the pressure, injuries, and battles behind Cleveland’s 2016 title. “Personally, I think it’s one of the hardest championships ever in NBA history that we got to accomplish,” Irving said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/yU2HQsPUPd

recent.text: Kyrie Irving said Cleveland’s tribute gave him time to settle in and embrace the support during his return. “This one felt a lot different than the other times,” Irving said. Read more on @DALSportsJrnl: https://t.co/fGspc0ZX5j
